<cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 2:1">ib. II, 1</cite> <he>אם כיון לבו וכ׳</he>) that religious exercises require the intention (of complying with the law, and must be repeated if performed without such intention)? <cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 28b">R. Hash. 28ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>מצוות אין צריכות כ׳</he> the intention of compliance is not indispensable; <cite ref="Eruvin 95b:21">Erub. 95ᵇ</cite> <he>לצאת בעי כ׳</he> (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. notes 90 a. 100) in order to have complied with the law, intention of compliance is required.
<cite ref="Berakhot 13b:10">Ber. 13ᵇ</cite> <he>כ׳ בלא קריאה</he> meditating (on the Biblical passage to be recited) without audible recitation.
Ib. עד כאן צריכה כַּוָּנַת הלב up to this (sh’ma to eḥad) attention to the meaning is indispensable.

<cite ref="Megillah 20a:2">Meg. 20ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 6:6">Deut. VI, 6</cite>) <he>אחר כ׳ הלב הן הן הדברים</he> the value of ‘the words’ (the recitation) depends on the attention of the mind (devotion).
<cite ref="Chullin 31a:14">Ḥull. 31ᵃ</cite> <he>כ׳ לשחיטה</he> the intention to slaughter according to the ritual; opp. <he>לחתיכה</he>; a. fr.
